payload.prompt: Wir haben eine Rechnung über 5044 EUR an Bergwerk GmbH (Org.-Nr. 806819859) gesendet, als der Wechselkurs 10.51 NOK/EUR betrug. Der Kunde hat nun bezahlt, aber der Kurs liegt bei 11.20 NOK/EUR. Erfassen Sie die Zahlung und buchen Sie die Wechselkursdifferenz (agio) auf das korrekte Konto.

payload.goal: Register payment from Bergwerk GmbH for invoice of 5044 EUR and book the exchange rate difference (agio/currency gain) to the correct account due to rate change from 10.51 to 11.20 NOK/EUR.
success_checks: Invoice of 5044 EUR is marked as fully paid
Payment registered at rate 11.20 NOK/EUR (56492.80 NOK received)
Original invoice booked at 10.51 NOK/EUR (53012.44 NOK)
FX gain (agio) of 3480.36 NOK posted to currency gain account (e.g., account 8060 or equivalent)
No open balance remains on the customer ledger for Bergwerk GmbH
risk_notes: Invoice must already exist in Tripletex; if sandbox is empty, full bootstrap chain is required
Correct FX gain account must be confirmed (typically konto 8060 'Agio' in Norwegian chart of accounts)
Payment date and exact bank receipt date needed to determine correct rate — 11.20 NOK/EUR assumed from prompt
If Tripletex auto-calculates FX difference on payment, manual voucher may not be needed — verify system behavior
Organization number 806819859 must match existing customer record
EUR must be configured as a currency in Tripletex settings
Bank account in NOK receiving EUR payment must be set up for reconciliation
payload.suggested_first_action: Search for existing customer Bergwerk GmbH (org. 806819859) via GET /customer and locate the open EUR invoice of 5044 EUR via GET /invoice.

line_items.description: FX gain (Agio) – exchange rate difference: (11.20 - 10.51) * 5044 EUR = 3480.36 NOK

ordered_steps: 1. Verify/create customer Bergwerk GmbH (org. 806819859) via POST /customer if not existing
2. Verify EUR currency is enabled in Tripletex settings (GET /currency)
3. Locate or create the open invoice of 5044 EUR at original rate 10.51 NOK/EUR (booked value: 53012.44 NOK) via GET /invoice or POST /invoice
4. Register payment on the invoice at new rate 11.20 NOK/EUR (received: 56492.80 NOK) via POST /invoice/{id}/payment with paymentDate and amount in EUR
6. If Tripletex does not auto-post FX difference: create manual voucher (POST /ledger/voucher) debiting bank account and crediting agio account (e.g., 8060) for 3480.36 NOK
7. Verify customer ledger balance is zero (GET /ledger/account/balance or GET /customer/{id}/balance)
8. Confirm voucher and payment are posted and reconciled

Do NOT use other query params — they are not supported.

MUST include id and version from the GET response.
When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
ALWAYS search first if product_number is provided: GET /product?number=<number> — sandbox pre-seeds products.
Only POST /product if GET returns 0 results.
Use 'number' field for the product number (NOT productNumber).
priceExcludingVat sets the base price. Also set vatType={"id": 3|5|6}.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id}.
Set orderDate and deliveryDate (use today_iso from execution_brief).
When a product was created, ALWAYS include product={"id": product_id} on the orderline.
Use unitPriceExcludingVatCurrency for the price field.
Set vatType={"id": 3} for 25%, {"id": 5} for 15%, {"id": 6} for 0%.
For multiple lines, prefer POST /order/orderline/list for efficiency.
Pass orders=[{"id": order_id}] to link order.
Set invoiceDate and invoiceDueDate.
Bank account 1920 MUST be configured first (see bank account setup pattern).
Method is PUT, not POST.
ALL params are QUERY PARAMETERS — NOT in body: PUT /invoice/{id}/:payment?paymentDate=YYYY-MM-DD&paymentTypeId=XXXXX&paidAmount=YYYYY
Do NOT send a JSON body — send empty body or no body. ALL data goes in the URL query string.
Get paymentTypeId first via GET /invoice/paymentType — use the first result's id.
paidAmount is the full payment amount (e.g., 47200). For foreign currency, use paidAmountCurrency instead.
Method is PUT, not POST.
date is a QUERY PARAMETER: PUT /ledger/voucher/{id}/:reverse?date=YYYY-MM-DD
Do NOT send date in the request body.
Use query parameter sendType=EMAIL.

payload.headline: Payment registered and agio voucher created, but one scoring check failed (likely wrong agio posting side).
what_went_wrong: Check 2 failed — the agio voucher debited account 1920 (bank) instead of crediting it; agio should debit AR/customer account and credit 8060 (Valutagevinst), not involve 1920 again.
The agent created a manual agio voucher on top of Tripletex's auto-generated FX postings (disagio to 8070), potentially double-counting the FX difference.
GET /ledger/voucher with default date params caused a 422 validation error (date range issue), wasting one call before correcting the date range.
The agent noticed Tripletex auto-posted to 'Valutatap (disagio)' account 8070 but did not investigate or correct this before adding its own manual agio voucher.
what_worked: Invoice creation, payment registration, and agio voucher creation all succeeded (3/4 checks passed).
EUR currency lookup, order/orderline/invoice chain, and payment via PUT /invoice/:payment all executed correctly.
what_to_try_next: For the agio voucher, debit the accounts receivable (1500) account and credit 8060 — do NOT involve 1920 (bank) in the agio posting since bank was already settled in the payment voucher.
Check whether Tripletex auto-posts FX difference on payment; if it does, skip the manual voucher or reverse the auto-posting to avoid double-counting.
Fix the GET /ledger/voucher call by always providing explicit dateFrom and dateTo parameters to avoid the 422 date range validation error.
